subject: Optimize Toolkit: Pilot packaging, quantization & KV-cache concession request
messages:
From: Ava Reed <ava.reed@arborhealth.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@arborhealth.ai
Date: 2028-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot economics + technical ask: KV cache + INT8 quantization impact

Hi Marcus / Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Arbor's ML and platform teams were encouraged by the latency profile and the hinting you showed for prefix caching. Before we lock a 3-month pilot, procurement needs a clearer commercial and technical picture:

- If we enable KV prefix caching at the route level (expected 40–60% hit for our FAQ flows), what is the expected delta to per-token bill?
- You mentioned INT8 inference with the Optimize toolkit. Are there recommended model variants you validate for INT8 (regression risk / ROUGE/accuracy delta expectations)?
- For a short pilot (3 months, 200M tokens/month peak), can you provide an illustrative pricing slab and any precedent concessions?

Can you send an updated term sheet and a technical note on quantization caveats? Procurement will need that to sign off.

Thanks,
Ava
Head of Platform Partnerships
Arbor Health AI

Attachments: none
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reed <ava.reed@arborhealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics + technical ask: KV cache + INT8 quantization impact

Ava — thanks, great questions. Putting answers in-line and attaching a short pilot term sheet: pilot-term-sheet.pdf.

1) KV prefix caching delta to per-token bill
- Short answer: effective per-inference compute tokens can fall 25–45% depending on hit rate and average prefix length. For your estimated 40–60% hit range we model ~33% unit-cost reduction for TTI-sensitive chat flows (conservative).
- Notes: savings appear as fewer decode tokens billed to the serving path when prefix is cached on the request path; there is a small additional storage and rehydration cost charged as a flat monthly fee in the Pilot Plus option (see term sheet).

2) INT8 quantization guidance
- We support two recommended INT8 modes in the Optimize toolkit: dynamic post-training INT8 (lighter risk, ~5–8% throughput uplift) and static calibrate-and-quantize INT8 (more aggressive, ~1.5–2x speedups on supported kernels).
- For clinical NLU tasks we recommend validating on the same prompt set (we can run a 2k-prompt regression with your evals). Typical quality delta: <2% F1 drop for our curated Llama-based variants; edge cases can exist for very long context or loosely formatted clinical notes.

3) Pricing slabs for a 3-month pilot (illustrative)
- Pilot Lite (no caching persistence): $0.018 /k infer-token, $0.0008 /k embedding-token; no commitment, limited support.
- Pilot Plus (KV caching + ops): $0.013 /k infer-token (assumes 40% cache hit), $0.0006 /k embedding-token; $3,000/month cache persistence fee.
- Concessions: for signed MAP and commit to a 6-month expansion we can offer a 12% commercial concession on Pilot Plus rates and 60% off onboarding services.

Next steps: I attached the pilot-term-sheet.pdf with line items and suggested MAP milestones. Happy to jump on a short call to walk procurement through the line items.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot-term-sheet.pdf
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reed <ava.reed@arborhealth.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-07-25T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics + technical ask: Pilot concession framing

Ava — quick commercial note to pair with Marcus's technical breakdown:

- We can accept a shorter pilot commitment but need lead indicators: a signed MAP and a short SOW for success metrics. If Arbor signs to a 3-month pilot + MAP (clear usage milestones), we can offer a one-time 8% launch concession on Pilot Plus pricing and waive the first-month cache persistence fee.
- For a 6-month forward commit we can stretch to the 12% concession Marcus mentioned and reserve a small pool of dedicated throughput for your peak windows.

I'll leave the technical caveats to Priyom, but commercially we want to keep the runway to expansion clear — if Arbor hits engagement milestones we convert to a reserved band and lock the discount.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-v2.xlsx (pricing and milestone tracker)
From: Tom Riley <tom.riley@arborhealth.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ava Reed <ava.reed@arborhealth.ai>
Cc: procurement@arborhealth.ai
Date: 2028-07-27T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics + technical ask: KV cache + INT8 quantization impact

Team — thanks. Procurement has a couple of asks before legal will accept the pilot term sheet: 

1) We need SOC 2 or ISO evidence and a short note on data residency for prefix caches (we're in US-East primary).
2) We'd like to propose a per-month spending cap (hard cap) during the pilot with an overage alert at 80% of cap. Can you commit to a hard cap mechanism?
3) We've attached suggested contract redlines (redlines.docx) focusing on indemnity and data handling for cached prefixes.

If you can respond with the SOC evidence and confirm hard cap tooling, we can route to legal. Also — is DocuSign possible for the MAP and SOW?

Regards,
Tom Riley
Senior Procurement Manager
Arbor Health AI

Attachments: redlines.docx
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Tom Riley <tom.riley@arborhealth.ai>, Ava Reed <ava.reed@arborhealth.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-07-30T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics + technical ask: KV cache + INT8 quantization impact

Tom — quick technical confirmation and operational caveats. Attaching a short technical note (quantization-caveats.pdf) and an updated MAP (MAP-v2.xlsx).

Responses:
- SOC2 / Data residency: Redwood can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and our data residency controls. KV cache persistence is region-aware and we can pin cache storage to us-east-1 for your pilot. Legal: we'll provide the SOC2 redacted report; technical contact can hand off full evidence under NDA.
- Hard cap: we support a hard spend cap on the tenant with automated throttling and overage alerts at 80%/90%. For the pilot we'll configure a $15k/month cap (configurable) and will surface alerts to your procurement and to our ops Slack channel.
- Quantization caveats: dynamic INT8 is the lowest-risk path for early pilot; static calibrate-and-quantize yields the best latency gains but requires a calibration corpus and a short validation window (we recommend a 5–10k-example calibration run). We'll commit to a 2k-regression test on your eval set prior to flipping to static INT8. See quantization-caveats.pdf for performance numbers and known failure modes (long-context drift, rare token hallucination risk in extremely low-temp decodes).

Operationally we accept your redlines on cache residency with minor edits — Marcus / Ben will follow up on commercial redlines and plan for DocuSign for MAP + SOW. Proposed next: legal to exchange redlines, ops to schedule calibration run the week of Aug 7.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: quantization-caveats.pdf, MAP-v2.xlsx
